corrections.text: The summary says "LinkedIn says not all of that is the engine" and the Overview says LinkedIn says "the improvement cannot be completely attributed to the migration to the new engine", both placed against the fall in infra failures from 925 to 63. In LinkedIn's post that caveat is written about the total failures remaining constant in absolute terms (11,175 in May 2025, 10,023 in May 2026) despite 3.7x the deployments, because error classification and reliability in the deployment orchestrator also improved. For the infra-failure count the post says only failures "completely attributable to the deployment stack" were included and drift errors were excluded on both sides. InfoQ describes the caveat more broadly ("the improvement isn't solely due to the new engine").

The headline's "Infra Failures" means the post's "deployment infra failures": failures due to the deployment system, excluding application, controller and invalid-manifest failures and, on both sides, drift errors. It is not LinkedIn's total failure count, which was 11,175 in May 2025 and 10,023 in May 2026.
